title: Chapter 25: The Voice of Deep Resentment doesn’t Vanish
content:
Chapter 25:

Thy Grave, Immortal Resentment

How many times has it been now that my consciousness has been dominated by this blankness?

Faced with a spectacle beyond comprehension before his eyes, Subaru stood frozen, at a loss for words, just as he had done again and again.

He had been beaten down. Countless times until now. He wanted to whine, just once, that surely it was about time he could be saved.

After all, he had witnessed nothing but tragedies, repeatedly, over and over like this.

Directly in front of the frozen Subaru, a blue-haired girl lay on the bed.

Her face, devoid of vitality, was pale, and her closed eyes would never open again. Her thin negligee—likely sleepwear—though strange to say at a time like this, suited her well, giving her a childlike air compared to her usual capable impression.

Suddenly, Subaru realized he had never seen her in anything other than her maid uniform. And the first time he saw her in other clothes, they were her final outfit.

“Why… is Rem…”

Muttering, Subaru thrust his hands into his hair, looked down, and muttered again.

Faced with a situation he couldn’t understand, his head, spinning uselessly in circles, hurt terribly. Perhaps it was also the fatigue from lack of sleep. Thinking felt awfully troublesome.

In each repetition, four times in total. For Subaru, who had been killed in three of them, she was the person he had to be most wary of as a perpetrator.

Roswaal, who could order her to silence him, and Ram, who likely shared the same position, met the same conditions, but there was no doubt he had judged Rem to be the biggest obstacle this time based on the experience of actually having his life taken.

Therefore, this time he kept them at a distance, even talked the reluctant Beatrice into getting involved, and postponed the situation again and again to prolong his life.

As a result, being able to greet the morning of the fifth day was good news, but…

“Why have our positions changed so much…?”

It should have been Rem trying to kill Subaru. Absolutely not the reverse, and he couldn’t think of a reason for Rem to be killed either.

Suddenly, Subaru stepped forward to confirm if she was truly dead. The girl laid on the bed had her hands clasped over her chest; her death face was peaceful, as if someone had cleaned it up.

He reached out, trying to touch that unmoving body. But,

“——Don’t touch her!”

His hand was slapped away by an arm swung with vigor, and Subaru groaned quietly and looked up.

Facing him across the bed was Ram, clinging to Rem and shedding tears. While continuing to shed tears that showed no sign of stopping, Ram said,

“Don’t touch Rem… don’t touch Ram’s little sister.”

It was a word of rejection leaving absolutely no room for argument.

Saying only that as if slamming it down, Ram clung to Rem’s body again, whispering to her while weeping quietly. It was a devoted and painful figure, like a mother telling a bedtime story to her sleeping child.

Even with her sister’s appearance inviting such pity, there was no sign of the younger sister waking up to rebuke her.

The pale profile, the lips with poor color. And the body that had stopped its beating.

Seeing those things up close, Subaru finally accepted reality.

—Rem had truly died.

“It is likely due to magic, I’d saay. Though it seems closer to a curse than magic.”

To Subaru, who had left the room with tottering steps, Roswaal, standing next to the door, voiced his deduction.

Raising a finger, the man with indigo long hair slightly tightened his usually completely lax expression, and said,

“The cause of death is debilitation. Her vitality was stolen while she slept, her heartbeat was slooowly distanced, and just like that, the flame of her life was blown out as though settling into stillness”

At the word “curse,” Subaru raised his face.

It was a deduction he remembered hearing. And regarding the cause of death Roswaal spoke of, Subaru also had an idea.

That was exactly the type of abnormality Subaru had experienced in the situation of his second death. Assuming that was likely the cause of his first death as well, then Rem’s cause of death this time would be the same as Subaru’s first time and indirect second time.

It would be, but,

“I was sure that debilitating magic was Rem’s doing, though.”

The second time, where he was debilitated by magic and had his skull crushed by an iron ball.

If one recalled that situation, Subaru couldn’t be blamed for predicting it was the crime of the same offender. However, in reality, Rem had been given death by a curse, and Subaru had thus slipped through not only the influence of the curse but also the baptism of the iron ball.

In other words,

“The curse and Rem are separate…? What about a cooperative relationship?”

In the case of his second cause of death, it was an attack after being affected by debilitation due to the curse. It would be natural to assume they were working together, but what about this case?

Falling out, Subaru thought, then shook his head. In the first place, he didn’t know the position of the curse user. Speaking from conditions, it would be strange if the curse user wasn’t someone close to the mansion.

Otherwise, they couldn’t have opportunities to contact Rem, and above all, they had to be a person whose motives and conditions overlapped with Rem’s actions.

Considering the remarks in the third iteration, Rem trying to kill Subaru to silence him was because she thought it would be for Roswaal’s sake. That act, which indirectly led to the elimination of an obstacle for Emilia, was the gift of loyalty, albeit excessive.

Therefore, the premise that he might not be able to avoid it, which had also mentally cornered Subaru, was greatly shaken because of the link with the curse user.

Unable to establish a logic that convinced him no matter what, Subaru, touching his chin and thinking, couldn’t hide his irritation. With the accumulation of fatigue, the blood circulation in his head right now was the worst.

Even knowing that no decent conclusion would come out, Subaru, who could do nothing but think, had to think. And so,

“Don’t tell me, a cooperative relationship is also X-ed out and they’re completely separate cases…?”

What if there was no relationship whatsoever between Rem and the curse user?

The first time, Subaru was targeted by the curse user and died just like that. The second time, Rem killed Subaru, who had fallen under the curse user’s spell, for some reason. The third time, Rem killed Subaru purely out of a rampage born of loyalty. The curse user was unrelated to this.

And this fourth time,

“Because I didn’t do anything, Rem became the curse user’s target…?”

The causal relationship was unknown. In the first place, even the reason why Subaru’s life was targeted by this curse user or whatever remained unclear. Or perhaps the curse user’s aim could be considered the people in the mansion in general, but then he couldn’t come up with a reason why those of low position like Subaru and Rem would be prioritized as targets, omitting important figures like Roswaal and Emilia.

In the end, it was going in circles unless the identity of the curse user was revealed. Feeling his thoughts blocked on all sides and stagnating, Subaru clicked his tongue in irritation and cut off his thinking. Then,

“You seem to be worrying quite seriously, don’t youuu?”

From a slightly higher position, Roswaal looked down at Subaru and muttered that. His blue and yellow odd eyes were narrowed as if appraising Subaru, and Subaru furrowed his brows at the unpleasantness of having his inner thoughts naturally seen through.

Perhaps realizing his own bad manners, Roswaal immediately corrected his posture, bowed to Subaru with his eyes, and said,

“Excuse me. It seems I am also a little on edge. As expected, when I think that a servant I favor has been made to meet with such a fate, well.”

Even while voicing an apology, Roswaal’s attitude never softened in the true sense. He crossed his arms, and while tapping his crossed arms lightly with a finger, said,

“Roast with fire, violate with water, carve with wind, sink into earth. —I feel like it wouldn’t be a return gift unless I did about that much. It’s awkward to ask this, buuuut… My Esteemed Guest, do you have any idea what happened here?”

There was not a fragment of a joking ring contained in those words muttered in a low voice.

Voicing a threat that was likely his raw true feelings, Roswaal stared at Subaru as if testing him. Suddenly, Subaru became aware of how bad the situation he was placed in was, and agonized over how to respond. But there was a voice that interrupted before Subaru could open his mouth.

“Last night or so, you said to be vigilant. You said that, right, Subaru?”

Looking up in the direction of the voice, what entered the vision of Subaru, whose eyes widened in astonishment, was a gray cat moving its short arms as if washing its face—Puck.

To Subaru, who was left speechless by his unexpected remark, Puck tilted his head and said,

“Emotionally and in terms of obligation, I would very much like to take your side, you know. But if I prioritize that and misjudge things, there’s a child who won’t be rewarded.”

Turning his black eyes softly toward the room, Puck rubbed his pink nose with his hand.

While maintaining his usual comical attitude, he must still have had thoughts regarding Rem’s death. Making small movements, he shifted and said,

“If lingering regrets or hesitation remain, the soul will fall to evil without being saved. For me, that is a sad thing, not only as a mere spirit, but as someone who had interacted with that child no little.”

Shaking his small head side to side, Puck curled his body up again as if to say he had said what he wanted to say. Gently watching over him on her palm, Beatrice was also staring at Subaru silently.

What kind of emotion was contained there? Even though she was such an expressive girl, the current Subaru couldn’t even verify that.

“…Subaru.”

Emilia pulled on Subaru’s sleeve anxiously, turning moist eyes toward him as if appealing for something.

If there is something you know—thoughts conveyed by just a single call.

While he wanted to throw his whole soul into answering her plea, the impulse to brush away her clinging to him was also Subaru’s true feeling.

If there is something you know—everyone says it lightly.

But if that were true, that was something Subaru wanted to scream in a louder voice. Indeed, if there was someone who knew the truth of the situation, he wanted them to come forward right now. And he wanted to slam all the countless questions floating up like mountains against them, and have them pull him out of this dead end with no exit.

However, in reality, such a convenient mastermind would not show themselves, and the meaning of the four pairs of eyes directed at Subaru would not change either.

The advice to Puck, given with good intentions, had backfired like this this time. Toward Subaru, who didn’t put it into words despite knowing something, even Puck must have harbored distrust. It was natural for Emilia, who had a deep connection with that Puck, to also harbor not a little suspicion toward Subaru.

He repeated loops, and struggled each time hoping for it to get better. However, the result was that every time he did one thing, it backfired and brought back a worse situation than imagined. Surrounded by enemies on all sides; how many times did Subaru have to repeat this to taste the same heartache Subaru felt last time?

“Subaru.”

Clearly, Emilia called his name.

It was proof that she harbored suspicion she couldn’t wipe away at Subaru’s attitude of falling silent. Subaru felt a sense of sorrow at her natural reaction as he continued to think.

In a situation tantamount to knowing nothing, how could he speak to convince them? Or perhaps, he thought they would be disappointed in Subaru, who knew nothing.

Thoughts that had become a messy jumble.

The moment he thought he wanted to say it and just get it over with—

The stagnation of the world and the black mist—as if induced by Subaru’s resignation, they eroded the world again, feeding on his resignation.

He lost his words. No, the lips that would utter words did not move a twitch.

Naturally, his hands, feet, eyes, and tongue didn’t move, and even the air was completely cut off from the world. Sound and movement were lost; at the return of the absolute space of silence and suspension, Subaru was literally struck dumb.

It was the unreasonable phenomenon that had forcibly cut him off the other day when he decided to tell Emilia about “Return by Death.”

The black mist created a black arm faster and more elegantly than before. That hand, which had been from wrist to elbow before, appeared forming the outline of a slight upper arm.

Just like last time, the arm slipped into the chest of the frozen Subaru without showing any sign of hesitation. Then, softly stroking his internal organs and sternum, it reached his heart, and—

—Instantly, his thoughts were blown away, and pain that could cause instant mental death pierced through his entire body.

“Subaru!?”

Hearing a grievous voice of sorrow, Subaru realized he had danced back to reality.

And that he was clutching his chest, a massive amount of sweat floating on his forehead, kneeling and breathing roughly.

Raising a hand lightly to the worried Emilia, Subaru looked back on the current phenomenon.

When he tried to tell Emilia about “Return by Death,” that black mist gave Subaru a warning in the sense of interfering with it.

And if it showed itself with a similar meaning this time too—

“Is it because it’s impossible to explain without touching on the content of the loop…?”

At least with his mental state just now, he didn’t think he could possibly dodge persistent questioning. But if that was true, this situation was the worst.

Subaru, who wanted to spill his guts, and the members who wanted to unravel Subaru’s guts. For the black mist, there could be no greater field of activity.

Endless questions meant endless torture. The moment he realized that, Subaru, in fear of the unbearable pain, trembled his lips and backed away.

That act,

“——If you know something, Ram won’t let you escape.”

To the girl who had collapsed crying in the room, looked like an unforgivable folly.

In a split second, a gust of wind shook the door of the room violently, slamming its aftermath against Subaru’s bangs. Immediately after closing his eyes at the natural storm,

“Ouch…!”

Sharp pain pierced his cheek, and Subaru instinctively covered his face with his palm. What he felt damply on his touching palm was the sensation of bleeding dripping from a wound just opened.

Realizing that was an injury from the wind just now, Subaru turned his surprise to the back of the room.

Gently stroking her sister lying on the bed, and directing the hand opposite that one toward him, the pink-haired girl glared at Subaru with eyes harboring rage.

“If you know something, spill everything.”

“Wait, Ram! That’s…”

Only the folly of saying “I can’t” was something he restrained himself from.

The moment he said that, it would become absolutely impossible to settle this situation. However, even if he stopped himself from saying it, not a single word to break the deadlock came out.

Subaru didn’t know what would become the trigger to receive that warning again.

The fear of that pain made him lose the ability to make correct judgments regarding Ram.

As a result, Subaru’s words petered out, failing to extinguish her momentum.

Toward Subaru, who shut his mouth, Ram sent out wind with the meaning of a second warning.

If a cliché expression was permitted, it was truly a phenomenon one would call a “wind blade.”

It was likely magic related to wind. The magic creating a sickle-weasel flashed with sharpness like a slash, tore through the walls and doors on the path to reach Subaru, and was about to slam in a blow like the one that tore his cheek—when it suddenly vanished.

Subaru and Ram, surprised and choking on their words. Between those two,

“——It is my policy to keep promises, in fact.”

Muttering, the one who stood in front of Subaru was the girl with cream-colored hair.

Beatrice lightly waved her raised palm, and without boasting about erasing the sickle-weasel Ram unleashed as if it were nothing,

“While in the mansion, Betty will protect this human’s safety, I suppose.”

“Lady Beatrice…!”

At Beatrice declaring so as if bored, Ram bit her lip in indignation.

Glancing sideways at her attitude, Beatrice looked up at the tall figure standing beside her, and,

“Roswaal. Your servant is acting rudely toward your guest, in fact. As the master of the mansion, how do you judge that, I wonder?”

Directed at him, Roswaal furrowed his brows for just a moment. But he immediately regained his usual composure, closed one eye and shrugged,

“Indeed, it is truly regrettable. If possible, I would also like to renew my welcome to him as a guest immediately. If he would spill what is in his chest and unburdened himself, then immediately.”

“…This guy was in Betty’s Forbidden Library last night, in fact. So he should be unrelated to this affair, I suppose.”

“Whether one should place weight on the situation is no longer the issue. Beatrice, surely you are fully aware of at least thaaat much, are you nooot?”

Negotiations broke down, and Roswaal turned the palms of both hands upward just as he shrugged. In those palms, he suddenly saw multiple colorful radiances floating up.

Even Subaru, who had absolutely no knowledge of magic, was made to realize that it was a state where condensed magic power was visible.

Red and blue, yellow and green—four colors of pale light floating; even if he didn’t understand just how outside the norm that was.

At Roswaal’s performance, Beatrice gave a small snort with her cute nose,

“As always, a dexterous youngster, in fact. Having a little bit of talent, putting in just a tiny bit more effort than others, and being blessed by lineage and a teacher by only a slight margin… Do you think you were able to escape being a jack-of-all-trades with just that level, I wonder?”

“You’re the one who is as harsh as always. Although, if I said I’ve never thought I wanted to try out just how different I, who continues to walk, am from you who spends time in a room where time has stopped—that would be a lie.”

A rise in magic power occurred between the two, bringing Subaru an illusion as if the atmosphere were distorting.

Unknowingly, the two heightened their fighting spirit, leaving Subaru, the person involved, behind.

Subaru himself didn’t know why it was turning out like this. However, the fact that he couldn’t utter words to stop the two was also a fact Subaru himself could only grit his teeth at.

“Howeeever, to think you would go so far as to physically protect him. Did you take quite a liking to him?”

“Keep the jokes to your fetishes, Roswaal. Betty’s ideal is Bubby himself, in fact. With that human, both adorableness and furriness are unsatisfactory, I suppose.”

Against Roswaal heightening the visible four-colored magic, Beatrice took no particular action while maintaining a calm stance.

However, around the girl who should have just been standing there, an overwhelming phenomenon that distorted space was occurring, which Subaru, standing close by, could sense.

That was merely the aftermath of gathered power; just imagining how much efficacy that power would display if it had directionality made his spine freeze.

“Why go this far?”

“A contract is absolute, I suppose. If I break it, Betty will no longer be Betty, in fact. Being sincere to a contract takes priority over everything else, I suppose.”

Responding to Roswaal’s sigh like that, Beatrice continued with “However,”

“If he aimed for this situation and used the contract with Betty, he would be an outrageous imposter, I suppose.”

“I…! I didn’t intend for that…!”

Glancing at Subaru, Beatrice looked away with emotionless eyes.

What Subaru wished from her was strictly because he regarded the phenomena related to the causes of death so far as dangerous.

He absolutely did not wish for a situation like this.

“It doesn’t matter, all of that doesn’t matter!”

Stamping her foot, it was Ram who interrupted that exchange.

Receiving everyone’s gaze, she gripped the hem of her skirt tightly,

“Don’t get in the way, let Ram through. Rem’s enemy… if you know something, tell everything. Save… Ram… save Rem…”

A grievous appeal, but Subaru had no words to return to it.

What was given to his silence was an invisible blade harboring rage and disappointment. However, that was again intercepted without reaching Subaru,

“I’m sorry, Ram. Even so, I will try believing in Subaru.”

Lining up next to Beatrice, it was Emilia who checked Ram.

She turned her palm toward Ram, and while carrying Puck on that shoulder, walked up to Subaru. Then, looking down slightly as if searching for words,

“Subaru, please… If you can save Ram, save Rem, please tell us everything.”

At the emotion of affection contained there, Subaru felt his own pettiness and was ashamed.

Even when things had come to this, Emilia was trying to stand by Subaru’s side. For Subaru, who hadn’t shown a decent attitude in this loop, and even now kept his mouth shut about the crucial matter and wouldn’t speak.

And also at his own weakness, unable to return a single thing to such consideration of hers.

“Sorry—”

Leaving that behind, Subaru let himself back away, putting distance between them.

For an instant, Emilia’s hand reached out to stop him. Before it could reach Subaru, it had to be turned to intercept the wind blade that was unleashed, and as a result, no one on the spot could stop Subaru’s feet.

“Subaru—!”

Shaking off the voice calling him to stop, Subaru cut through the corridor regardless of appearance. Behind him, even while feeling a clash of magic power occur, he didn’t even summon the courage to look back.

Despite Emilia racking her brains for him so much, Subaru didn’t have the courage to face that fear.

He was weak. He was helplessly fragile. That was why he was scorning every kind of goodwill and good intentions, and running away selfishly.

He didn’t know what to do anymore.

Where he should go, how he should think, everything.

Only—

“——

I will absolutely kill you

!!”

Hearing from behind, the scream of a girl like she was vomiting blood.

Only the scream of vengeance of the girl who lost half her body, tearing at herself, chased after him.

As if fleeing, fleeing from that, covering his ears, shaking his head, raising a voiceless voice, Subaru threw everything away and ran.

He continued to run.
